# Channel scoreboard — per-channel, per-work-class track record

Feeds routing decisions (delegation-protocol R5) and the harness `priors` hook.
Score = verifier score in [0,1]. Update at every task close-out. Retirements
(w≥3 failures on a class) recorded in the notes column with date + reason.

| Channel | Work class | Attempts | Mean | Recent scores (new→old) | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| QA agent (fleet, Testing Agent MAIN) | **Pass 21** — through-code on Datasec/NexusAI **S30's fix round** at `3dda4ec` against `11cdf5a` (2026-09-04 06:10→06:34, 23m37s; static, no browser, zero writes, tree clean at both ends) | 1 | **1.00** | 1.00 | **Proved every closure by RE-RUNNING the exact mutation that found it, green baseline first, failing set predicted before each tamper — three tampers, three exact matches.** **Replaced Wednesday's own instrument with a better one unprompted:** it distrusted a path filter and compared git SUBTREE OBJECT HASHES plus a full `ls-tree` diff including modes, which a rename or mode change cannot defeat — **so the zero-pixel claim keeping Kam's frames valid is now proved by a stronger instrument than the one that made it.** **CORRECTED ITS OWN PASS-20 SEVERITY IN THE OPEN, unprompted: F-5 Minor → Major (F-10), because `verify-suite.sh`'s floors ARE the CI gate — 73 of 83 suites and 1 039 of 1 403 tests can vanish with the build green — and red-proofed it BOTH directions.** Also gated `ea6378d` and `4aabad0` itself to settle a figure rather than asking. Found the standing class three times inside the fix round, including **a both-off assertion that CANNOT FAIL inside the fix for a check that could not fail.** Held the builder's NOT-CLAIMED line rather than letting a green stand for a render. |
| Datasec/NexusAI agent | **S30** — the bounded fix round on pass 20's F-1…F-6, wrapped at `3dda4ec` (2026-09-03 18:0x→18:37Z) | 1 | **0.80** | 0.80 | **All three Majors genuinely closed at the mechanism level**, each proved by its own mutation; F-3's whole sentence and denominator re-derived; F-4 red-proofed three ways; both F-6 instances found (it found the SECOND itself). **CORRECTED WEDNESDAY'S BRIEF AND WAS RIGHT** — 'assert every case flips to 1' would have required asserting a falsehood; its per-family formulation is the right definition of isolation and the tester would defend it. **Its second red-proof — 'a parser that can no longer find its subject must not report a pass' — VERIFIED, and it is the first time this fleet got AHEAD of an apparatus-displaces-subject defect rather than behind it.** `DATED_WINDOW = 500` genuinely measured; both bounds named load-bearing; NOT-CLAIMED boundary stated honestly ('1403/83 is evidence about code and prose, not about a page'); RD-291 filed with its own gap written down. **−0.20: F-8 (Major) — F-2 narrowed 57.6% and NOT closed, the guard's own negative-control wording 357 chars from a real date still leaves the suite fully green · F-7 the both-off clause cannot fail · F-11 the F-6 correction reproduces F-6 (one SHA, two verdicts in adjacent rows) · F-9 an anchor unique only by a line-wrap accident.** F-10 is NOT its debit — pre-existing, and its honest 'nobody has red-proofed this' is what got it closed. |
| QA agent (fleet, Testing Agent MAIN) | Through-code on Secuura/Blockchain **#800's SECOND fix round** at `7e6621bb1` (+ **#806**) (2026-09-04 06:10→06:33, 22m58s; static, read-by-SHA, zero writes, no real `.env` read, `rm` never used — two fixtures QUARANTINED instead) | 1 | **1.00** | 1.00 | **Fourteen of seventeen tampers matched the failing set it wrote down BEFORE running them**, label-for-label. **R2-3 exists only because it checked its own mutation had fired** — without that second step it would have banked a green and no finding, which is precisely the trap the builder had disclosed falling into. > **(1) Seeded `*123` accounts vs unique credentials on the dev box.** The stack ships
> demo's seeded logins; scanners were probing the host within MINUTES of 443 opening.

> ## 🔴 NEW 2026-08-20 ~08:4x — Secuura: does Stuart's "$5000 Founders credits live"
> actually move the 6 Sep expiry? (portal-only check, ~2 min, YOUR eyes)

> 6 Sep expiry** — and 6 Sep has been the only dated clock on Kintsugi. The credits
> API 404s for the scoped SP (verified 08-19), so only the portal billing view can
> answer: do the $5000 credits REPLACE/extend the expiring grant, or sit alongside
> it? **Ask: one look at the billing view.** Until you rule, every record keeps the
> 6 Sep clock standing — s50 flagged it precisely so the screenshot does not silently
> read as "the clock moved."
